text:
arya: Quick heads-up — planning a midweek maintenance window for rolling node reboots and network firmware updates across eu-west2 + us-east1. Thinking Wed 02:00-05:00 UTC, split cohorts to avoid cross-region capacity crunch. Need: capacity impact estimate, backfill plan, and customer comm draft. @sam can you run numbers? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sam: Yep. I'll run current pool utilization + queued jobs and return a table. My initial thought: stagger 30% of each pool for 45m each, with 15m warmup for KV cache. That keeps tail latency low. Also recommend canary in us-east1 first.

mike: Two asks: 1) check reserved vs shared GPU assignments — we should avoid touching Dedicated pools that customers pay for. 2) cost hit: if we use burst spare capacity or preemptible backfill, estimate +200-300 GPU-hours. Who owns the cost?

sophia: Note: eu-west2 egress is near quota Tue nights due to backups. If we trigger large KV reseed / cache-warmup across region at 02:00 UTC we might spike egress and hit throttles. Suggest moving eu-west2 cohort to start at 03:00 UTC, so it's outside backup window. Also needs net team signoff for fw updates (ping @netops).

devops-bot: Maintenance ticket created: MT-2026-2143. Scheduled: 2026-03-25 02:00-05:00 UTC. Owners: arya (overall), sam (capacity), mike (customer impact), sophia (network). Link: https://redwood.example/maint/MT-2026-2143

sam: Quick plan sketch — cohorts and commands: 
```
# cordon + drain (cohort A)
kubectl cordon gpu-node-az1-0
kubectl drain gpu-node-az1-0 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
# after warmbackfill
kubectl uncordon gpu-node-az1-0
```
We'll use backfill policy `conservative` (max 20% burst). After each cohort we seed KV cache for 10-15m: run small synthesis jobs to warm cache.

mike: For SLA customers on Dedicated pools: don't evict. We should route their active sessions to fallback region if available. If not, notify customers and offer temporary credits. I'll model cost of credits once sam posts GPU-hours.

sophia: From netops: "we can move the eu-west2 window to 03:00 but need a short maintenance ACL for the firmware push (5m per rack). We'll provide BGP guard rails." — they asked for exact rack list by EOD.

sam: Capacity numbers (rough): eu-west2 active GPUs 1,200 (usable), us-east1 active GPUs 2,400. If we cordon 30% cohorts sequentially with conservative backfill, expected lost capacity at peak ~720 GPUs across both regions but distributed. Backfill + burst adds ~280 GPU-hours.

mike: OK that's acceptable. Recommend we use our cost reserve (ops-burst fund) to cover the 280 GPU-hours for backfill. @finance FYI if this is final.

arya: Decision: split window into two sub-windows to avoid overlap: us-east1 02:00-03:30 UTC (canary then main), eu-west2 03:00-05:00 UTC (staggered start). Owners as devops-bot ticket. Action items:
- sam: produce per-cohort exact node lists + backfill scripts by EOD
- sophia: get rack list for ACL + netops signoff
- mike: draft customer-facing notice and credits policy
- oncall rotation: notify @oncall team and post incident playbook in the ticket

sam: Will post node lists + `drain.sh` (with retry/backoff) in the ticket. Example snippet I'll include: 
```bash
# drain.sh (simplified)
for n in $(cat cohort-a-nodes.txt); do
  kubectl cordon $n && kubectl drain $n --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data || continue
  sleep 900  # warmbackfill
  kubectl uncordon $n
done
```

mike: I'll draft the customer note and share in #support-distro. Short version: "planned infra maintenance, potential degraded throughput for non-dedicated workloads, dedicated customers unchanged". cc: legal for wording.

sophia: Netops asked to confirm the firmware version list; uploading to MT ticket now. Also: if egress triggers, have fallback policy to slow KV reseed.

arya: Good. Let's keep comms tight. If anything changes, update MT-2026-2143 and ping here. :thumbsup:
